title: Annotatio V §.IX: Reformed teach spiritual presence/sacramental; external≠internal communion — stop before §.X
pass_a_gloss: The Author again at the start of paragraph XVII slides back from the Oral Eating disputable between us to the fabricated dispute about the presence of Christ’s body in the Supper and its true and real Sacramental Eating, about to seek his only stronghold here; and since the presence of Christ’s body in the Supper, and this sacrament’s true and real Eating, is analogous to the Communion of Saints, he persuades himself he has already then accomplished all he intended — not remembering that both the Presence of Christ’s body in the Supper and true real Sacramental Eating, but each Spiritual, are most constantly taught by the Reformed: which meantime alone, not the Oral, is heard as the fountain and spring of the Communion of Saints celebrated in the Apostolic Symbol and contradistinguished from the Article on the Catholic Church. Hence beside the point in this place the Author discriminates between External and Internal Communion; when the prior is not of the Saints inasmuch as they are holy, but pertains to the Catholic Church, in which saints and unclean hypocrites are contained alike, yet they do not alike enjoy the Saints’ Communion strictly so called and internal.
pass_b_english: The Author (§.XVII) again slides from Oral to a fabricated fight over presence and true real sacramental eating as his only stronghold — forgetting the Reformed constantly teach both as Spiritual.

Spiritual presence/eating alone is the fountain of the Creed’s Communion of Saints (vs the Catholic Church article). External church communion holds saints and hypocrites together; internal Saints’ communion they do not share alike. Stop before §.X.
source_text: Autor rursus initio paragraphi XVII. à Manducatione Orali, inter nos disputabili, ad commentitiam de præsentia corporis Christi in Cœna ejusque Sacramentali verâque & reali Manducatione, disputationem relabitur, hîc præsidium suum unicum quæsiturus; & quoniam corporis Christi præsentia in Cœna, hujusque sacramentalis vera ac realis Manducatio, Communioni Sanctorum analoga est, se jam tum omne id confecisse sibi persuadet, quod intenderat, haud memor, tùm Præsentiam corporis Christi, in Cœna, tùm Manducationem Sacramentalem veram realémque, sed utramque Spiritualem, à Reformatis constantissimè doceri: quæ interim sola, non verò Oralis, Communionis Sanctorum in Symbolo Apostolico celebratæ, Articulóque de Ecclesia Catholica contradistinctæ, fons audit & scaturigo. Hinc præter rem h. l. inter Communionem Externam, & Internam, discriminat Auctor; quando prior Sanctorum non est, quatenus sancti sunt, sed ad Ecclesiam Catholicam pertinet, in qua sancti, & immundi hypocritæ, juxta continentur, non autem juxta Sanctorum Communione strictè sic dictâ & interna fruuntur.
notes: §.IX: spiritual fountain; external vs internal; before §.X.
